candidate_signal_below_deadline.description: Occasional single-stall dark time in the authority `prepare` route (max 1513.85ms; r1) and in the dispatch gap between deadline creation and route entry (max 1749.49ms; r2), plus sub-deadline response slowness with the 12th (final) request consistently slower (e.g. 793ms r4). All terminal service internals (provider_lookup, provider_probe_*, terminal_open, terminal_stop, session_list) stayed sub-ms.
candidate_signal_below_deadline.not_attributed: Correlates with the authority audit-write path rather than terminal logic, but attribution is NOT claimed; these are recorded as sub-deadline phenomena, far below 5000ms.
candidate_signal_below_deadline.recurrence_classification_contribution: Consistent with (but not proof of) environmental contention during the original RED; the original bursts (~5.0s) were an order of magnitude larger and were not reproduced.

classification_basis: The preserved RED was NOT reproduced in 4 controlled runs (0 recurrences). Non-reproduction does NOT explain or clear the preserved RED.
Original RED cause remains UNKNOWN; no source defect identified OR excluded in this round, no harness defect identified or excluded, environmental contention remains plausible but unproven.
A sub-deadline stall signal (authority prepare dark time) was captured and preserved for future diagnosis, but is not attributable by current evidence.
Instrumentation is persistent, dormant, deadline-neutral, and now ships with the suite so any future recurrence is captured at stage granularity.
